reinvestment_runway_detail.tam_source: NVIDIA management, spoken (Jensen Huang on earnings calls and at Goldman Sachs Communacopia, reaffirmed 2026; CFO Colette Kress): $3-4T annual AI infrastructure spend by 2030, midpoint used
reinvestment_runway_detail.independent_tam_source: Dell'Oro Group, Data Center IT Capex 5-Year Forecast (July 2025): ~$1.2T worldwide data center capex by 2029; cross-check Gartner: $1.48T AI infrastructure spend in 2026 (out of $2.67T total AI spending)
reinvestment_runway_detail.rationale: NVIDIA's own figure is $3-4T (midpoint $3.5T) of annual AI infrastructure spend by 2030, stated by Jensen Huang and reaffirmed in 2026. Dell'Oro's independent estimate is ~$1.2T of data center capex by 2029, and Gartner puts 2026 AI infrastructure spend at $1.48T. NVIDIA's figure is about 3x Dell'Oro's, which is a meaningful gap, mainly because NVIDIA counts all AI infrastructure (power, facilities, sovereign and enterprise AI) while Dell'Oro counts data center capex only. Chip-only estimates are much smaller: GM Insights $154.6B in 2026 and Grand View $578B gen-AI chipsets by 2033. The SEC-filed RPO of $3.2B as of 2026-07-26 was not needed as a proxy because a company TAM exists; it is tiny next to either market figure and mostly reflects software/service contracts, so it is a weak demand signal.

reinvestment_runway_detail.tam_source: None published. Alphabet management (Q1 and Q2 2026 earnings calls) only says, without a number, that selling TPUs into customer data centers expands its addressable market
reinvestment_runway_detail.independent_tam_source: WPP Media, This Year Next Year 2026 Global Midyear Forecast (global ad revenue 2026, $1.3T); cross-check: Gartner public cloud end-user spending ($723.4B in 2025, ~ $850B in 2026 per a secondary source)
reinvestment_runway_detail.rationale: Alphabet gives no dollar TAM. On the Q1/Q2 2026 calls, management and CFO Ashkenazi only said that selling TPUs into customer data centers expands its addressable market. So the demand proxy is the SEC-filed backlog of $519.5B as of 2026-06-30, which matches the $514B Google Cloud backlog stated on the Q2 2026 call. Independent figure: WPP Media puts 2026 global ad revenue at $1.3T (excl. US political), which fits Alphabet's ad-led revenue. Dentsu's estimate is lower at $1.06T. For Cloud, Gartner puts public cloud end-user spending at $723.4B for 2025; the ~ $850B 2026 figure comes from a secondary source citing Gartner. With no company TAM, there is nothing for the independent figure to diverge from. The backlog equals about 40% of the 2026 ad market and about 60% of 2026 cloud spending, but it covers multiple years. Adding ads and cloud gives ~ $2.1T, but the definitions differ, so only the ad figure is used as the headline.
